name: Citizenship by Registration (Continuous Lawful Residence)

requirements.blocker_text: 7 years of continuous lawful residence in Kenya immediately preceding the application, holding a valid permit throughout.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 7 years of continuous lawful residence under a valid permit.

requirements.blocker_text: Physically resided in Kenya for the 12 months immediately preceding the application.
Must understand and speak Kiswahili or a local dialect.
requirements.fix_path: Demonstrate proficiency in Kiswahili or a recognized local dialect.

requirements.blocker_text: Must demonstrate a substantive contribution to the progress or advancement of Kenya in some area of national development.
Must not have been convicted of an offence and sentenced to imprisonment for 3 years or longer.

evidence_required.document: Proof of continuous lawful residence (7 years) under a valid permit
Evidence of substantive contribution to national development

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: 7 years' continuous lawful residence under a valid permit, including the 12 months immediately preceding application

sources.title: Kenya Law (official government legal database) -- Kenya Citizenship and Immigration Act 2011, Section 13: registration after continuous lawful residence requires 7 years' residence under a valid permit (including the 12 months immediately preceding application), Kiswahili or local-dialect proficiency, knowledge of Kenya and citizens' rights/duties, no 3+ year criminal conviction, and a substantive demonstrated contribution to Kenya's national development

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Kenya). Published on tier-1 sourcing (Kenya Law). The Act itself does not use the word 'naturalisation' -- this route is legally 'registration after continuous lawful residence' under Section 13, distinct from Section 11's marriage-based registration (see ke_citizenship_by_marriage.json), though both share the same 7-year figure. DISTINCTIVE REQUIREMENT NOT SEEN ELSEWHERE IN THIS DATASET IN THIS EXPLICIT A FORM: an applicant must demonstrate a substantive contribution to Kenya's national development, not merely reside lawfully and behave well -- a more affirmatively merit-oriented standard than the largely passive residence/character/language tests used by most other countries built in this dataset. dual_citizenship_allowed TRUE, consistent with Kenya's constitutional and statutory dual-citizenship allowance (see ke_citizenship_by_descent.json notes).
